items.title: Arnold Dix says Nepal rescue teams face challenge unlike any before
items.blurb: The Australian tunnel expert, who arrived in Kathmandu on Saturday, joined Nepali and Indian teams searching for people believed to be trapped inside the Chilime hydropower tunnel.

items.title: Floods wash away 1,806 hectares of farmland, threaten food supplies
items.blurb: Bhotekoshi floods are expected to cut food production by 7,686 tonnes in affected areas.

items.title: Nepal moves against online abuse targeting flood survivors
items.blurb: Cyber Bureau forms 10-member team to identify users posting hateful and demeaning comments about people affected by the Bhotekoshi floods.

items.title: Mental wellbeing: How to help without feeling helpless after the floods
items.blurb: From donating and sharing useful information to taking a break from distressing coverage, small actions can help us move beyond helplessness.

items.title: People in flood-hit Rasuwa villages call for help after supplies run out
items.blurb: Residents of Aamachhodingmo Rural Municipality who have lost family members look up for help when they hear a helicopter fly. Their prayers mostly go unanswered.

items.title: Flood sends hydropower shares tumbling, but damage is uneven
items.blurb: The Bhotekoshi floods have hit a handful of listed hydropower projects, yet shares across the sector, and in insurance, have fallen as investors grapple with uncertainty over losses, claims and reconstruction.

items.title: Former Reconstruction Authority chief Govinda Raj Pokharel on the urgent need for a permanent, powerful disaster ministry
items.blurb: Warning against compounding risks from clustered dams and melting glaciers, Pokharel calls for strict infrastructure codes, cross-border early warning systems with China and India, and a rapid pivot toward high-altitude…

items.title: When the ground disappears, the sky must be organised
items.blurb: Nepal needs to know how to use the helicopters it already has before the next disaster arrives.

items.title: The flood is over, the fear remains
items.blurb: Children who survived the August 26 flood are struggling with sleepless nights, panic, and memories of family members lost, while officials and aid workers race to address a quieter aftermath.

items.title: Power restored in much of flood-hit Rasuwa and Nuwakot, but pockets remain dark
items.blurb: The restoration is helping rescue and relief efforts. Solar units to reach settlements off-grid.

items.title: Kulman Ghising on the lessons Nepal must learn from the hydropower disaster
items.blurb: The former NEA chief discusses the damage to hydropower projects, lessons from the rescue operations and the design and safety reforms Nepal’s hydropower sector needs after the Bhotekoshi floods.

items.title: Eleven days without a call: Three Kanchanpur families wait for news of men missing in the flood
items.blurb: In Kanchanpur, wives, children and elderly parents are still waiting for relatives swept away or out of contact after the Bhotekoshi floods.

items.title: How an IT engineer used AI to aid Nepal’s flood response
items.blurb: Ministry of Finance’s Niraj Bhusal deployed an AI-driven web application to track casualties and streamline relief efforts, providing Nepal’s disaster management teams with a new tool for emergency coordination.

items.title: Nepal, South Korea discuss flood rescue, disaster recovery and climate finance
items.blurb: Nepal seeks continued South Korean support for flood recovery as the two countries call for greater international action on climate-related losses.

items.title: Prithvi Highway collapse leaves Pokhara’s tourist buses idle as air traffic soars
items.blurb: The Krishnabhir landslide has disrupted 150 tourist buses on the Pokhara-Kathmandu route, pushing daily air passenger numbers towards 3,500 and prompting tourism operators to explore an alternative route across the…

items.title: Scan, tap, done: How digital payments are changing disaster relief in Nepal
items.blurb: A decade after the 2015 earthquake, mobile banking and QR payments have made it possible to raise over Rs10 billion for flood victims in days.

items.title: Reporter’s Diary: I went back to Rasuwa. The river had changed everything
items.blurb: Fourteen months after covering the first Lhende Khola flood, I returned to the same disaster zone. This time, roads and homes were gone, families were searching for their loved ones, and the places I remembered were…

items.title: Flood damages four houses and bridge in Gorkha
items.blurb: A pre-dawn flood in remote Chumnubri Rural Municipality destroyed four houses and swept away a bridge, with no casualties reported.

items.title: Kathmandu supply lines rerouted after floods block main highway
items.blurb: Fuel, food and other essentials are reaching the Capital through alternative roads, but transport disruption is pushing up prices and limiting cooking gas supplies.

items.title: Nepal is draining four glacial lakes. Scientists say it is not enough
items.blurb: Risk assessment, early warning systems, outlet management and cautious building in the path of a potential flood matter just as much.
